$comment: Gemfall beat 7, the Collection's chapter 7 (docs/campaigns/gemfall.md, 7H). Defines facet_caravan, which 07r and 07l also grant. Summit: scene_tree_line's two choices set climbed_the_mountain or walked_away; the lost-fight setback sets climbed_the_mountain. Cult and clock are both decided once, at scene_tamsins_offer: sell (funded_the_break + clock_late), refuse (refused_the_cult), or hand the stones back (refused_the_cult + clock_steady). The setback path never reaches that scene and sets clock_late itself. The Walk is the Collection's own exit from the campaign, and it lives here: after the tree line a walking party plays the epilogue in this chapter (the walk_ scenes) and its endings carry endsCampaign, so the campaign completes without a chapter 8. A walking party never enters the mountain. Pacing episodes on the spine (the price board, the rival collector, the mosshorn calf, the humming night, the checkpoint, the boy on the milestone, the bend approach, Professor Tidewell, the dawn bell) set only chapter-local flags and leave cult, clock and the Walk untouched.
title: The Collection

plate.narration: At the Pinch, buyers crane their necks toward the next caravan. A dragonling climbs her ladder for a better look. The bend ahead is crowded already. Getting there first will take more than a loud voice.

objectives.label: Won the Caravan Stone at the worst bend
Gave a stone back, even though nobody made you
Saw that the gem deposit was really a crab

goal.text: Beat three other crowds to the caravan's loudest stone at the worst bend.

steps.label: Race the other crowds for stones

facet_caravan.name: The Caravan Stone
facet_caravan.text: The masterpiece stone of the fattest caravan. It hums so loud the mules wear earmuffs.

scene_like_weather.narration: The realm reads you now. A mosshorn sniffs your packs and quietly leaves. A silence follows you like a dog nobody feeds. Ahead, every road squeezes into the Pinch, a gap between two red hills. You told Pellam you would finish the collection. So here is the plan. Beat three other crowds to the caravan's loudest stone at the worst bend.

scene_like_weather_listen_silence.narration: Your bigfoot listens to the silence the way others listen to a song. It is a circle a mile wide, and you stand right in the middle. "They're not scared of us," your bigfoot says. "They're scared of what we carry."

scene_price_board.narration: At the Pinch stands a price board as tall as a house. A dragonling girl called Bryony is up a ladder with chalk. Each time the ground shrugs, she writes a bigger number. "Up again!" she sings. Your pack hums along.

variants.text: "Humming pebbles," Bryony says kindly. "Everybody starts with those."
"Only {facets} of the big ones," says Bryony. "Everybody starts somewhere."
Bryony's chalk snaps in half. "Nobody has {facets}!"

check_price_board.prompt: Read a price board that changes every time the ground shrugs

onSuccess.narration: Every time the ground shrugs, prices jump. But the loudest stones are the cheapest: buyers think the humming means they are cracked. Nobody here knows what you know. You do the sums, and grin.

onFailure.narration: The numbers change faster than you can read them, and a puff of chalk dust sets you sneezing. Bryony laughs so hard she nearly falls off her ladder, and throws you down a stick of chalk, for luck.

scene_price_board_ask.narration: Bryony slides down. "Anything that hums sells," she says. "Hessa's singers in bark masks pay double. The wardens take it for nothing. Grandmother says don't sell at all." She looks at your packs. "You're the weather people. Everybody's talking about you."

scene_price_board_sums.narration: You came north to get rich. You add up your packs at today's prices, and you have to sit down. Bryony brings you water. Then she writes a brand new number at the top of the board, just to see.

choice_the_race.narration: Three other crowds want these stones: wardens with numbered boxes, grandmothers with knitting, and singers in bark masks. The masks are Hessa's friends from the soup tent, the Deep Hollow. They want to wake the mountain so it can fix things, so they buy every stone. How do you get ahead?

choice_the_race_camps.narration: You push into the camps and start trading. Your first deal is a stone for a honeycake, which should not work, and does. By the third deal, people come looking for you.

choice_the_race_nobody_knows.narration: Nobody knows what you are for, so nobody stops you. A warden walks right past. A grandmother nods as if you were one of hers. A mask offers you soup. You take the soup.

scene_warden_pass.narration: You told the wardens the truth, and they still trust you. A clerk stamps a pass for you and waves you through without checking your bags. The stamp feels heavy on your hand all afternoon.

scene_grandmother_look.narration: A grandmother stares at your bulging packs over her knitting. She does not say "No, dear." She says nothing at all. Then she hands you a warm bead, because it is cold up there.

scene_grandmother_look_give_one.narration: You put a stone in her basket. The needles stop. "Thank you, dear," she says softly, and closes your fingers around the warm bead. "It remembers who was kind." Then the needles start again.

scene_grandmother_look_thank.narration: You thank her and walk on. Her needles click faster. Twenty steps later you look back. She is still watching your packs, and she has not blinked.

scene_rival_collector.narration: In the camps you meet a rival. Lady Fleecewick is a sheeple in a lace collar, pushing a glass cabinet on wheels. Forty stones sit inside on velvet cushions. "Collectors! How lovely. I'll trade you my best for your loudest."

variants.text: "Humming pebbles," she says kindly. "Mine started that way too."
"{facets} of the real ones," she murmurs. "A lovely start, dear."
"{facets}," she says faintly. Her forty cushions suddenly look small.

scene_rival_collector_trade.narration: Her best stone is pink and shy. Your loud one hums so hard in her cabinet that every label falls off. "Marvelous," says Lady Fleecewick, and gives you a luckstone too, for the noise.

check_rival_collector.prompt: Out-talk a sheeple who has been collecting since before you were born

onSuccess.narration: You admire her cabinet so knowledgeably that she goes pink to the tips of her wool. In the end she will not trade at all. She gives you a luckstone, just for the conversation, and asks you to write.

onFailure.narration: You haggle hard. She haggles harder. By the end you have traded nothing, agreed to everything, and promised to visit her cabinet at home, which apparently has a room of its own. She seems delighted.

scene_rival_collector_pride.narration: Lady Fleecewick cleans her glasses and looks again. Then she sits down hard on her own cabinet. "Oh my," she says. She does not ask to trade. She only asks, very politely, to draw it.

scene_road_gifts.narration: A warden runner brings a note from Pellam's citadel ledger: your names, and COLLECT, with a question mark. Under it: STILL? Then the road starts bringing back things you did on the way here, as if the realm kept your receipts.

scene_ossley.narration: A frog in a very old hat poles a flat boat up a dry creek. OLD OSSLEY is painted on the side: the frog from the reeds of the Great River. His boat is piled with lost stones. "Stones want to go home," he says. "Which way are you going?"

scene_ossley_debt.narration: Ossley takes a long time to answer. His price was never coin. "One stone you didn't find," he says. "Give it to the boat. That's all."

scene_mosshome_runner.narration: A MossHome runner jogs up with grumbling mules, loaded with everything the Woods took from careless hunters. Your knotted cord says some of it is yours. She counts the knots, then your packs, slower.

scene_mosshome_runner_send_home.narration: "Take them back to the Woods," you say. The runner grins so wide the moss in her hair wiggles. She ties a new knot in your cord. "The record likes a surprise!"

scene_mosshome_runner_claim.narration: You claim it all. The runner unloads every shovel and hat and humming stone. "The record will know who has these," she says, and jogs off without looking back.

scene_boggart.narration: A boggart with a satchel of scribbled paper sidles up, not looking at you. "Catalog," it tells nobody. "Who bought what in the marsh. Costs one really good sentence you overheard."

scene_boggart_grandma_said.narration: You repeat what Grandmother Tull said about the bell nobody rings, even the part she said twice. The boggart closes its eyes to listen. "Lovely," it tells nobody, and lets go of the catalog.

scene_boggart_wardens_said.narration: "It hums!" you shout in Dunmore's exact voice. The boggart shivers with joy and writes it down twice, once backwards. "That's a keeper." It hands over the catalog, still not looking at you.

scene_ford_witch.narration: It is Mother Thrum, the witch from the ford, with a ringing wool sock under one arm. "I always ask twice," she says. "Once at the ford, once at the mountain. What do you actually want?"

scene_ford_witch_dont_know.narration: Mother Thrum's face goes soft. She ties a songbird ribbon around your wrist. "That's the first true thing anyone's said on this hill," she says. "I'll ask again. I always do."

scene_ford_witch_all_of_them.narration: Mother Thrum does not sigh, which is worse. She puts a ringing stone from the ford in your hands. "Then here is one more. Mind it doesn't ring you to sleep."

scene_mosshorn_calf.narration: Past the camps, a mosshorn calf has lost its mother. It is all knees and moss and worried noises. Its mother calls from the ridge, but she will not come closer. She can hear your packs.

scene_mosshorn_calf_packs_down.narration: You set the packs down and carry the calf over, taking turns at the wobbly end. Away from the packs, the mother trots right up. She licks whoever carried the calf, very wetly, from chin to eyebrow.

check_mosshorn_calf.prompt: Coax a lost mosshorn calf along a trail of moss

onSuccess.narration: Moss, moss, moss, all the way up the ridge. The calf follows it, nibbling, and walks straight into its mother's side with a happy bump.

onFailure.narration: The calf ignores the moss and follows you instead, everywhere, like a shadow with knees. In the end you walk it all the way up the ridge, packs and all, and its mother is so cross with you that she forgets to be frightened.

scene_mosshorn_calf_ask_mother.narration: Your unicorn touches noses with the mother, and she lets the calf come home. "She isn't scared of us," your unicorn says. "She's scared of the sound. It sounds like the mountain waking up."

scene_evening.narration: Evening. Campfires pop up all along the road. The ground shrugs more often than this morning. Nobody pitches a tent near yours.

scene_evening_count.narration: You lay your stones out in one long glittering line. They hum at each other.

variants.text: You count the real ones first. None. The rest are rush gems, loud and ordinary. A mule sniffs the line, unimpressed.
You count the real ones: {facets}. One rush gem keeps rolling to the end to be counted again.
You count the real ones: {facets}. Nobody at the Pinch has a line like this. People stand back with their hats off.

scene_centaur_relay.narration: A centaur relay canters past your fire without stopping. They have heard what you are for. "Fat caravan tomorrow," one calls over her shoulder. "We're sending it the long way. Around you."

scene_centaur_relay_fair.narration: She looks surprised you did not argue. She slows for a step, as if to say more. Then she canters on into the dark, and the dust settles on your humming packs.

scene_centaur_relay_old_way.narration: You call after her the old road-people way, palm up, from far off. She skids to a stop. A manticore keeping the old courtesy! "Fine," she says. "Past you. Once. Don't make me sorry."

scene_relay_sing.narration: The centaur relay singers at the campfires sing about wagons that have not come yet, so you hear tomorrow's traffic tonight. A grandmother's runner hands you a list of caves nobody may dig. To a collector, it looks like a treasure map.

scene_ember.narration: "Darlings!" cries Madame Coralie Fenn from her barrel on wheels, tied to a caravan roof. She has the warm red stone you sold her on the quay, your very first. Now it sits in a velvet box labeled THE FIRST FACET, and its price has gone way up.

scene_ember_too_much.narration: You wave. Madame Fenn waves back with both arms, and her barrel wobbles. "Next time, darlings!" she calls. The caravan rolls on, with your very first stone humming on top.

scene_ember_buy_back.narration: You pay. Madame Fenn hugs the velvet box before handing it over. "I always hoped it would be you, darlings." The Ember Facet is warm as toast, and it hums as if it remembers you.

scene_humming_night.narration: Nobody can sleep. The stones hum loud and all together, like a choir warming up. A mule in the next camp holds its hooves over its ears. Somebody shouts, "KEEP IT DOWN!"

scene_humming_night_socks.narration: Every sock you own, and two you borrow. The stones hum on inside, like bees in a pillow. It is quieter, but not quiet. You fall asleep at last with very cold feet.

check_humming_night.prompt: Sing a whole pack of humming stones to sleep

onSuccess.narration: You sing the softest song you know. Slowly the stones find your note and hum along, then softer, and softer, until they are only purring. Three tents away, somebody says thank you.

onFailure.narration: You sing. The stones love it. They hum along at the tops of their voices, and the mule joins in, and the camp three tents away joins in too, and soon everybody is singing and nobody minds about sleep at all.

scene_humming_night_glade.narration: You set the Glade Stone in the middle of the pile. It hums low and slow, like wind in leaves. One by one, the other stones hush around it. The mule takes its hooves off its ears.

rest_lonely_camp.narration: Nobody camps near you. Your stones hum low and sleepy, like a cat that is far too big. Patch each other up. Tomorrow comes the worst bend on the north road.

scene_checkpoint.narration: Halfway up the north road, wardens have built a checkpoint: a gate, a table, and a clerk with two stamps. "Everything that hums goes in a numbered box," he says. Stamp, stamp. Everyone in line is hiding stones in their hats.

scene_checkpoint_declare.narration: You wait an hour, then set it all on the table. The clerk's eyes go wide. He stamps and logs it twice, keeps one stone "for the seal," and hands you a receipt. Even the receipt hums.

check_checkpoint.prompt: Everybody scramble round a warden checkpoint over loose scree

onSuccess.narration: Up the scree and round the gate, quick and light as goats. Nobody sees. Well. One goat sees. It does not tell.

onFailure.narration: Halfway round, the scree starts to slide, and so do you, all the way down into the checkpoint line, right at the front. The clerk looks at you, sighs, and waves you through, because the paperwork for this would take all day.

scene_checkpoint_pass.narration: The clerk sees yesterday's stamp and waves you through without looking up. A boy in the line watches your humming packs go by untouched. His mouth falls open.

scene_milestone_boy.narration: Past the checkpoint, a boy in a coat three sizes too big sits on a milestone. His name is Alder. He holds out one humming stone. "Will you buy it? I need the fare home. Mom says the mountain is no place for us now."

scene_milestone_boy_buy.narration: You pay a fair price, and a bit more. Alder counts the coins three times, beams, and runs for the wagon. His stone hums in tune with yours at once.

scene_milestone_boy_fare.narration: You pay his fare and fold his fingers back around his stone. "But you're the collectors," he says. "Everybody says." You tell him everybody says a lot of things. He waves all the way down the hill.

scene_milestone_boy_fresh_start.narration: You came north for a fresh start too, and you tell him so. Alder listens with his whole face. "Then I'll keep mine till I'm bigger," he says, "and come back for my own." He shakes your hand like a grown-up.

scene_milestone_boy_walk_down.narration: You can't buy it, and you say sorry. You walk Alder to the wagons anyway. A drover lets him ride on the tailboard for a song. It is a very long song, and soon the whole wagon is singing.

scene_roadside_glitter.narration: Just before the bend, two big glittering lumps sit on a warm patch of road. Prospectors grab at them, then run back without them. The lumps look just like gem deposits. They also have legs.

check_crabs.prompt: Read what the glittering lumps are trying to tell you

onSuccess.narration: They are glassback crabs, and they are waving their claws in the most polite warning in the realm: this is our warm spot. You walk the long way round, and they wave you off like aunties.

onFailure.narration: You step a little closer to get a better look, which turns out to be exactly the wrong thing to do.

encounter_crabs.narration: The gem deposits stand up. They are glassback crabs, and this is their warm spot.

onVictory.narration: The crabs clatter off sideways, grumbling.

onDefeat.narration: The crabs shove you into a ditch. Half your packs burst open, and the masks scoop up what rolls out.

scene_bend_approach.narration: Around the last corner is the worst bend, and you are not first. Wardens stack boxes. Grandmothers set out stools. Masks tune up. Far below, the fattest caravan crawls up the zigzags. You have a little time.

scene_bend_approach_mules.narration: You walk beside the lead mules for a mile. They wear cotton in their ears against the hum. You scratch ears and whisper nice things. Now the lead mule thinks you are its favorite people in the world.

check_bend_approach.prompt: Everybody scramble up a crumbly rock for a look inside the caravan

onSuccess.narration: From the top you can see into every wagon. Eleven are full of pots, pans and grumpy passengers. The middle one holds a single crate, nailed shut, and the canvas above it is trembling. Now you know exactly where to stand.

onFailure.narration: The rock is crumblier than it looks. You come down faster than you went up, in a little landslide of your own, and land at the feet of a grandmother, who hands you a cookie without a word.

choice_the_bend.narration: The worst bend is a hairpin over a long drop. Here comes the fattest caravan. Wardens wait with boxes, grandmothers with knitting, masks with sacks, and you. Four crowds, one wagon, and in it the masterpiece stone, humming.

choice_the_bend_axle.narration: Your bigfoot has been listening to the silence, and it has a wobble in it. The middle wagon's wheel is coming off! You shout just as it does. The crowds jump back. You catch what rolls out.

choice_the_bend_crowd.narration: Your kitsune whispers to a warden about grandmothers, to a grandmother about masks, and to a mask about wardens. Soon all three crowds are shouting at each other. The middle wagon stands alone, with you beside it.

choice_the_bend_buyers.narration: Thanks to the boggart's catalog, you know who bought this stone and for how much. You say both numbers out loud. The caravan master goes pale, then laughs. "No point haggling with somebody who's read my post."

choice_the_bend_relay_owes.narration: The relay pays its debts. The fattest caravan swings around the hairpin on the wrong side of the road, right to you. The centaur leading it never looks at you. "Once," she says to the air.

choice_the_bend_early.narration: You heard this caravan in last night's song, so you reach the hairpin an hour early and sit where the lead wagon must stop. The caravan master looks at you, then at the crowds puffing up behind. "First come," she shrugs.

choice_the_bend_mule_whistle.narration: You whistle. The lead mule's ears pop up through the cotton, and it turns toward you. The whole caravan turns after it. "Fine," sighs the caravan master. "The mules have decided. What's your offer?"

choice_the_bend_middle_wagon.narration: While three crowds rush the lead wagon, you wait by the middle one. The caravan master climbs down right in front of you and blinks. "How did you know?" You tell her you looked. She sells you the crate on the spot.

choice_the_bend_loud_offer.narration: You offer what a loud stone fetches at the Pinch, which is not much. The caravan master has had a headache since this stone came aboard. "Take it," she says. "Please. Take the noise."

check_bend.prompt: Outbid three other crowds for one humming wagon

onSuccess.narration: Your offer is so good, and so fast, that the caravan master shakes your hand before anybody else has finished shouting.

onFailure.narration: While you are still counting, a masked wagoneer quietly steers the middle wagon off up a side track. The masterpiece stone is gone, and the masks have it.

scene_caravan_won.narration: The Caravan Stone is the size of a loaf of bread and hums like a whole choir. Every stone in your packs hums louder, as if they know each other. The ground shakes once in reply.

scene_tidewell.narration: Everyone is coming down the road but one: a selkie with ink on both elbows. PROFESSOR TIDEWELL, says her notebook. She is the scholar who told the Exchange the gem-light fell upward. "Wait," she says, and listens to your packs like a doctor.

variants.text: "Not one of the real ones," she whispers, and winks. Then she mutters about "the eighth one."
"I count {facets} of the real ones," she whispers. Then she mutters about "the eighth one."
"I count {facets}!" She steps back as if your packs were hot. Then she mutters about "the eighth one."

check_tidewell.prompt: Follow a very fast-talking scholar to the end of her theory

onSuccess.narration: She grabs a napkin and draws on it, very fast. "The eighth is the crown of the seal, the stone the whole arch leans on. It isn't lying loose, it isn't for sale, and taking it would be like pulling the lid off a jar." She folds the napkin into your hand. "I only ever wanted to be right," she says. "Not this right."

onFailure.narration: She starts to explain, talking faster and faster, and then the ground shakes, and her notes fly off down the hill like startled birds. She runs after them, shouting back over her shoulder, "Whatever you do, don't PRY!" You never quite hear the rest.

scene_tidewell_show.narration: You lay the collection on a flat rock. Professor Tidewell walks down the line with one inky finger.

variants.text: "Rush gems. Lovely and ordinary. The real ones are still out there, and the eighth most of all." She pats a gem, as if it tried its best.
"{facets} of the real ones. A good start. But the eighth is still out there, the one that can't be bought."
She counts twice and sits down hard. "{facets}! I was right, and you found them." She hugs you.

scene_tidewell_ember.narration: You hold up the Ember Facet. Professor Tidewell laughs. "From the Exchange! I knew one came down there." She holds it to her ear like a seashell. "Same note as the others. Only louder. As if it's nearly home."

scene_tamsins_offer.narration: That night a woman in a bark mask sits at your fire and takes it off. It is Hessa, from the soup tent. "We'll buy what you traded for here," she says sweetly, "so we can break the seal properly, and fix it." She sets out thirty coins. Selling helps her break it sooner. Giving the stones back to the grandmothers buys the seal time. Either way, you still choose to climb or walk.

variants.text: Your great facets are not for sale.

scene_sold.narration: Hessa counts out every coin with care, and thanks you, and means it. She carries off the stones you traded for, sack after sack.

variants.text: Your rush gems she leaves. "Bring those to the mountain." As she goes, the ground shakes hard. Down the hill, a bell rope creaks.
Your great stones she leaves. "Bring those to the mountain." As she goes, the ground shakes hard. Down the hill, a bell rope creaks.

scene_handed_back.narration: Hessa puts her mask back on and goes. At dawn you carry the stones you traded for to the grandmothers' cairn. A grandmother wraps each one in wool.

variants.text: Your rush gems she will not take. "The mountain will want to hear those, dear."
Your great stones she will not take. "Those are for the mountain, dear."

scene_dawn_bell.narration: At dawn the ground gives its biggest shake yet. Down in the last dragonling village, the great bell's ribbon slips loose. The bell starts to swing. If it rings, every town will think it is the ring nobody says out loud.

check_dawn_bell.prompt: Catch a swinging bell rope before it rings

onSuccess.narration: You reach it in three bounds and hang on with everything you have. The bell swings, slows, and stops, one hair from ringing. A grandmother in a nightcap looks out of a window and nods at you, once.

onFailure.narration: You are one step too slow. The bell gives a single small tink. The whole valley freezes. Then a grandmother leans out of a window in her nightcap and shouts, "Just the wind, dears!" and everybody breathes again.

scene_dawn_bell_clapper.narration: You scramble up and hug the clapper. It is cold and smells of old pennies. The bell swings you back and forth like a very serious swing, then gives up.

scene_dawn_bell_ribbon.narration: You tie the bell up with your songbird ribbon, neat bow on top. The bell stops. The ribbon sings softly about staying quiet. It is the best-tied bell in the foothills.

choice_tree_line.narration: The tree line. Above, the mountain shakes in a slow, patient rhythm. Below, everyone runs south. Climb, and you reach the Keeper and choose what the stones are for. Walk, and your journey ends here.

rest_the_climb.narration: You climb the mountain everyone else is running from. At the top is the eighth stone, the one that is not for sale. The ground shakes with every step, and your packs hum louder the higher you go.

ending_robbed.narration: The masks are gone, and so is half your collection. The ground shakes in a slow, patient rhythm. You gather what is left and climb. The only stone still worth having is at the top, and you are far behind.

walk_scene_tree_line.narration: You turn south. Behind you, the mountain shakes. Ahead is the green, and everyone else running into it. Your packs hum so loudly you sound like a walking beehive.

walk_scene_tree_line_caravan_hum.narration: You let the Caravan Stone hum the loudest, as if it were leading. Once, the mountain answers: one long note you feel through your boots. Then it does not answer again.

walk_scene_realm_reads.narration: The realm reads you as you go. Jackalopes go silent a mile ahead. A pride of manticores walks a wide, polite circle around your camp. Even the moss leans away from the path, as if you were weather.

walk_scene_realm_reads_glade_hum.narration: You hold up the Glade Stone. Every leaf for a hundred steps goes still. The forest knows the sound of its own bruise. It holds its breath until you put the stone away.

walk_scene_realm_reads_ask_trees.narration: Your unicorn asks the trees, kindly, why they lean away. The answer comes in slow creaks. It is not you. It is what you carry away. The trees are not angry. They sound like someone watching a cart go the wrong way.

walk_rest_switchback.narration: You camp on a switchback where the rocks are still warm. Nobody says much. Share the last snacks, patch each other up, and listen to the mountain grumble behind you, farther away each hour.

walk_scene_factions.narration: On the caravan road, a centaur relay runner called Brisk trots up. "News, if you want it," she says. "Everybody up there is doing something." She looks at your packs. "Without you."

walk_scene_factions_close.narration: "Does anybody up there know what we know?" Brisk looks at you hard. "You knew," she says. "You knew, and you came down." She says nothing else. She doesn't have to.

walk_scene_wardens_hold.narration: "The wardens did what you told them," says Brisk. "Checkpoints on every road. Every stone logged twice. It's ugly, but they're holding." A warden wagon rolls uphill, full of stones going home.

walk_scene_gatherers_hold.narration: "The grandmothers turned gathering law inside out," says Brisk. "Every stone that came down is going back up, carried by dragonlings with bells on their tails. It's slow. It's holding."

walk_scene_news.narration: "Nobody knows much," says Brisk. "The wardens are guessing. The masks are singing. Everybody's waiting for somebody to do something." She looks at your packs, then says nothing, which for a centaur is very loud.

walk_scene_boundary.narration: At the boundary stones, a dragonling grandmother sits knitting something long and red. "Take what the mountain drops," she says. "Never pry at what it holds." Then she holds out one hand, palm up, and waits.

walk_scene_boundary_thank.narration: You thank her and keep walking. Her hand stays out, palm up, long after you pass. You know, because you look back, and you wish you hadn't.

walk_scene_boundary_give.narration: You put a stone in her hand. She holds it against the red knitting. "Thank you, dear," she says softly. Behind you, a small bell rings a ring you have never heard. It is a happy one.

walk_scene_the_fuse.narration: The grandmother puts down her knitting. Up the mountain, every town's bells are counting. "Everybody knows what the last ring means," she says. "Nobody says it." She looks at you a long time, then knits faster.

walk_scene_the_fuse_give.narration: You give her a stone after all. Her needles stop shaking. "Well," she says. "That's one." The bells go on counting. But under them, one small bell rings a happy ring.

walk_scene_look_back.narration: At the bottom of the foothills you turn around one last time. Mount Red Sky glows against the evening sky. Somebody up there is doing the thing you decided not to do.

walk_check_send_word.prompt: Get a message about the seal back up the mountain in time

onSuccess.narration: A griffin courier takes your letter straight up into the smoke. By morning, the warden checkpoints are reading it aloud.

onFailure.narration: Your letter goes up with a caravan that turns around halfway, because caravans do that now.

walk_check_last_chance.prompt: Give your best stone to a dragonling runner heading uphill, and ask them to hurry

onSuccess.narration: The runner takes your stone and your message, and runs. You never learn their name. They get there.

onFailure.narration: The runner is kind, and quick, and just too late.

walk_ending_collectors.narration: The realm holds. Not because of you, but it holds. The last bell never rings. At home, people ask the troll's old question: and where is it going? You are still thinking. History calls you The Collectors, and leaves the next page blank, just in case.

variants.text: You walk out of the foothills with loud, ordinary rush gems and not one real facet. A light walk home.
You walk out of the foothills with {facets} of the real ones humming in your packs.
You walk out of the foothills with {facets} of the real ones, the biggest collection that road has ever seen.

walk_ending_not_there.narration: Behind you, the last bell rings. Far down the road, you watch the red sky grow redder from somewhere safe. The realm goes on, changed. History calls you The Ones Who Weren't There.

variants.text: You walk home with rush gems and a lot of quiet. But one stone has stopped humming. It points north like a compass, as if asking: try again?
You walk home with {facets} of the real ones. That is something. But one stone has stopped humming. It points north like a compass, as if asking: try again?
You walk home with {facets} of the real ones, and it does not feel like enough. One stone has stopped humming. It points north like a compass, as if asking: try again?

interaction_cabinet.narration: One wheel of Lady Fleecewick's cabinet sticks in a rut. Forty stones slide toward the low corner. "Lift, dears! Gently! They bruise!"

interaction.cue: Everyone lift or lower your side until the cushions are flat, then carry the cabinet.
interaction.objectLabel: A glass cabinet of forty stones

onSuccess.narration: Not one cushion slides. Lady Fleecewick gives you three coins. "Collector's courtesy. Don't spend it all on honeycakes."

onFailure.narration: The cabinet tips, and forty stones roll into a heap of lace. Nothing breaks. Lady Fleecewick sighs and waves you on.

onAssisted.narration: Not one cushion slides. Lady Fleecewick gives you three coins. "Collector's courtesy. Don't spend it all on honeycakes."

interaction_boxes.narration: Past the gate, a tower of numbered boxes topples off the clerk's shelf. He is too busy chasing them to ask how you got here. You help stack them back. He gives you a honeycake from his hat. "Only been in there since Tuesday."

interaction_hairpin.narration: The last wagons grind around the hairpin, right across the path you need. A mule in a little straw hat watches you think. Wait for a gap, then go.

interaction.cue: Tap when the gap between the wagons is wide open.

onSuccess.narration: You dash through with a wagon-length to spare. The mule in the straw hat nods, as if it timed you itself.

onFailure.narration: You go a heartbeat early. A wagon rolls so close it tips the mule's hat onto your head. Nobody is hurt. You cross on the next gap.

onAssisted.narration: You dash through with a wagon-length to spare. The mule in the straw hat nods, as if it timed you itself.

interaction_tidewell_knocks.narration: Professor Tidewell knocks the mountain's rhythm onto a rock. Thump, tap, tap, rumble. You listen together. "You may be the second person in the world to hear that properly," she says, and hands back her pencil. It was yours.

scene_echo_cutting.narration: The bell is quiet, but up the road two long gray shapes copy every sound, half a breath late. Tink, like the bell. Thump, like the ground. A grandmother in a nightcap puffs up. "Echo hunters, dears. They block the cutting, and your stones are the loudest thing for miles. Please make them lose the thread."

encounter_echo.narration: Two echo hunters unfold from the rock wall, copying your footsteps one beat late. Be louder than one sound, and stronger than an echo.

scene_echo_quiet.narration: The echo hunters fold back into the rock and sulk. The grandmother tucks a little whistle into your hand. "For calling a village when something copies you," she says. "Keep it."

scene_echo_lost.narration: The echoes pile up until nobody can think. Then the grandmother bangs two pots together, loud and honest. The echo hunters slink away. No whistle tonight, but the cutting is clear.

interaction_price_clues.narration: Bryony saves three chalk notes. A loud hum scares buyers. Scared buyers offer less. The lowest offer is on the loud wagon. Put them in order: what causes what? Bryony has chalk on her nose.

interaction.cue: Arrange cause, response, then the clue about the wagon.
clues: Buyers think the loud hum means a crack. They lower their offers.
The cheapest wagon is the loud one, not the quiet one.

onSuccess.narration: You spot the bargain: loud does not mean broken. Remember that at the bend.

onFailure.narration: The notes smudge. Bryony explains, but the bargain column changes before you can copy it.

onAssisted.narration: Bryony reads the notes with you. You copy the loud-wagon price before it changes.

interaction_wagon_watch.narration: From the rock you see a glow under one of three wagon covers. Track it as the wagons swap places. The lead mule looks up, as if checking your homework.

interaction.cue: Watch the glowing load, then choose its final position.

onSuccess.narration: You mark the right spot. The master will find you beside the stone.

onFailure.narration: The covers cross and you lose the glow. You can still try another way.

onAssisted.narration: A driver points out each wagon as it moves. You mark the right spot.

voiceGuide.tone: warm, glittering, a little lonely; the land treating the party like weather, never scolding; after the Walk: quiet, bittersweet, honest; the realm is never cruel to the walkers, it just tells the truth; always a spark at the end
forbidden: calling the party greedy or bad

npcVoices.hessa: Deep Hollow cell member who ran the soup tent; sweet, sincere, makes the arithmetic sound kind; says 'properly' a lot
npcVoices.old_ossley: very few words, long pauses that are not hesitation, answers the question you meant
npcVoices.grandmother: a dragonling grandmother at the boundary stones; knits, quotes the one rule, never says the thing everyone knows
npcVoices.mosshome_runner: breathless, cheerful, counts knots out loud, then counts packs
npcVoices.boggart: talks sidelong to nobody, never meets your eye, treasures overheard sentences
npcVoices.ford_witch: Mother Thrum, the ford witch; pointed hat, dry, kind underneath; only asks one question and means it
npcVoices.centaur_relay: brisk, proud of the roads, speaks over her shoulder at a canter
npcVoices.exchange_merchant: Madame Coralie Fenn, the Exchange gem-buyer in a barrel on wheels; delighted to see you, genuinely fond, calls everyone darlings, and still a merchant
npcVoices.caravan_master: exhausted, practical, will sell to whoever stops shouting first
npcVoices.brisk: Brisk, a centaur relay runner; fast-talking, fair, says a lot by saying nothing
npcVoices.bryony: a dragonling girl who keeps the price board at the Pinch; chalky, quick, nosy, cheerful
npcVoices.lady_fleecewick: a rival collector, a sheeple in a lace collar with a glass cabinet on wheels; gracious, thrilled by any stone, never sore about losing
npcVoices.alder: a boy on a milestone selling his one stone for the wagon home; polite, hopeful, trying hard to be grown-up
npcVoices.tidewell: Professor Marrow Tidewell, the selkie scholar from chapter 1; ink on both elbows, talks fast, draws on napkins, proud and worried at once

interaction_boxes.narration: Beside the checkpoint table, the numbered boxes are piling up faster than the clerk can stamp them. "You! Yes, you! Hands!" he cries, pointing at a long shelf by the road. The boxes have to go down the line hand to hand, and every single one is humming. The top one seems to be humming a song about lunch.

interaction.cue: Catch the box, then pass it down the line.

onSuccess.narration: Every box reaches the shelf. The clerk stamps the last one with both stamps at once, and pulls a honeycake out of his hat. "For the hands," he says. "It has only been in there since Tuesday."

onFailure.narration: One box slips and rolls downhill, humming happily, and three wardens chase it. The clerk sighs and stamps the rest himself, one stamp at a time.

onAssisted.narration: Every box reaches the shelf. The clerk stamps the last one with both stamps at once, and pulls a honeycake out of his hat. "For the hands," he says. "It has only been in there since Tuesday."

interaction_tidewell_knocks.narration: Before she hurries off, Professor Tidewell kneels and knocks on a rock with her pencil: a slow beat in three kinds of knock. "The mountain says it in this order," she whispers. "Watch it, and knock it back to me. Then I will know somebody besides me has heard it."

interaction.cue: Watch the knocks, then knock them back in order.

onSuccess.narration: Thump, tap, tap, rumble. Professor Tidewell writes it down with a flourish and says you may be the second person in the world to have heard it properly. Then she hands back the pencil. It was yours.

onFailure.narration: Your knocks come out a little tangled, and Tidewell writes down the tangle too. "Even a muddle is data," she says cheerfully. "Mine usually are."

onAssisted.narration: Thump, tap, tap, rumble. Professor Tidewell writes it down with a flourish and says you may be the second person in the world to have heard it properly. Then she hands back the pencil. It was yours.
